title: MIT Teacher Uses AI to Help Data Centers Use Less Power
summary:
Data centers are big buildings full of computers. They use lots of electricity and can make power grids work harder. Christina Delimitrou, a professor at MIT, wants to fix that by making the computers inside run smarter.

Her team uses machine learning so cloud systems waste less energy. They improve old software, share hardware more carefully, and design leaner servers. That way, companies can do more computing with the machines they already have.

Delimitrou says if data centers are not used well, they burn more power than they need. Cutting extra software "bloat" without slowing things down could mean fewer new data centers.

Earlier research found many large systems ran at only about 15 percent capacity. Machine learning can help manage thousands of machines better. Her work shows smarter software—not only more buildings—can meet growing internet demand.
why_it_matters: Apps kids use run in data centers, so saving electricity there helps the planet.
